claim: Hearing loss affects around 466 million people worldwide.
source: Hearing loss is the most common sensory deficit with estimates of around 466 million people affected worldwide (WHO, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to WHO, 2019

claim: Loss of sensory hair cells of the inner ear is the primary cause of sensorineural hearing loss.
source: Loss of sensory hair cells of the inner ear is the primary cause of sensorineural hearing loss (Bohne and Harding, 2000; Hinojosa et al., 2001; Géléoc and Holt, 2014; Wong and Ryan, 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: The organ of Corti develops from a post-mitotic, pro-sensory domain established in the developing cochlear duct between embryonic days E12.5 and E14.5 in mice.
source: The highly structured sensory epithelium of the inner ear, known as the organ of Corti, develops from a post-mitotic, pro-sensory domain established in the developing cochlear duct between embryonic days E12.5 and E14.5 in mice (Ruben and Sidman, 1967; Lowenheim et al., 1999; Chen and Segil, 1999; Matei et al., 2005; Lee et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Post-mitotic cells in the developing cochlear duct are the progenitors for sensory hair cells and their adjacent supporting cells.
source: These post-mitotic cells are the progenitors for sensory hair cells and their adjacent supporting cells (Fekete et al., 1998; Kelley, 2006; Driver et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Sensory hair cells function as mechanoreceptors that convert sound vibrations into electrical signals.
source: Sensory hair cells function as the essential mechanoreceptors that convert sound vibrations into electrical signals, which are then transmitted to the brain via the spiral ganglion neurons that innervate the hair cells (Géléoc and Holt, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: Hair cells within the organ of Corti are arranged into one row of inner hair cells and three rows of outer hair cells.
source: The hair cells within the organ of Corti are precisely arranged into one row of inner hair cells and three rows of outer hair cells, interdigitating with a variety of supporting cells; inner border, inner phalangeal, pillar cells, Deiters' cells and Hensen's cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in text and illustrated in Figure 1A

claim: Hair cells are susceptible to degeneration by genetic mutations and environmental stressors.
source: Hair cells are susceptible to degeneration by a variety of genetic mutations and environmental stressors, such as exposure to loud noise, ototoxic drugs including cancer chemotherapy and aminoglycoside antibiotics, aging and over 200 known syndromic and non-syndromic genetic loci conferring predispositions to hearing loss (Matsui et al., 2004; Cheng et al., 2005; Bodmer, 2008; Langer et al., 2013; Atkinson et al., 2015; Wong and Ryan, 2015; Vaisbuch and Santa Maria, 2018).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: In mammals, hair cells do not spontaneously regenerate.
source: In mammals hearing and balance are dependent on the maintenance of hair cells present at birth (Groves, 2010; Géléoc and Holt, 2014), since hair cells do not spontaneously regenerate (Roberson and Rubel, 1994; Chardin and Romand, 1995; Forge et al., 1998), and so their death leads to lifelong hearing loss and balance disorders.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Non-mammalian species such as birds and reptiles can spontaneously regenerate lost hair cells from existing supporting cells.
source: In contrast, non-mammalian species, such as birds and reptiles, are able to spontaneously regenerate lost hair cells from existing supporting cells, leading to full functional recovery (Corwin and Cotanche, 1988; Ryals and Rubel, 1988; Stone and Cotanche, 2007; Brignull et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Atoh1 expression is both necessary and sufficient for the induction of sensory hair cells in the embryonic and neonatal cochlea.
source: Within the inner ear, expression of Atoh1, a bHLH class transcription factor (Lo et al., 1991; Ross et al., 2003) is both necessary and sufficient for the induction of sensory hair cells in the embryonic and neonatal cochlea, and ultimately plays an integral role in initiating the hair cell gene expression program (Bermingham et al., 1999; Zheng and Gao, 2000; Woods et al., 2004; Kelly et al., 2012; Chonko et al., 2013; Cai et al., 2013; Ryan et al., 2015; Scheffer et al., 2015; Stojanova et al., 2016; Costa et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Atoh1 expression alone is not sufficient to induce hair cell differentiation in somatic cells.
source: However, previous studies have shown that Atoh1 expression alone is not sufficient to induce hair cell differentiation in somatic cells (Izumikawa et al., 2008; Costa et al., 2015; Abdolazimi et al., 2016), or mature supporting cells of the organ of Corti (Kelly et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012b).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: The combination of Six1, Atoh1, Pou4f3, and Gfi1 (SAPG) can convert mouse embryonic fibroblasts into induced hair cells.
source: To this end, we have identified a cocktail of four transcription factors, Six1, Atoh1, Pou4f3, and Gfi1 (SAPG), capable of converting mouse embryonic fibroblasts, adult tail tip fibroblasts, and postnatal mouse supporting cells into induced hair cells (iHCs).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript

claim: SAPG transduction activated Atoh1-nGFP with a 35% efficiency in MEFs.
source: Overall, SAPG transduction activated Atoh1-nGFP with a 35% efficiency, and nearly 80% of all Atoh1-nGFP positive cells also expressed MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin (Figure 1D).
evidence: Quantitative data from experiments shown in Figure 1D

claim: 78.4% of SAPG-transduced cells that activated Atoh1-nGFP also expressed MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin.
source: The majority of SAPG-transduced cells that activated Atoh1-nGFP also expressed MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin (78.4% ± 1.9) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Quantitative data from experiments shown in Figure 1C and 1D

claim: iHCs successfully upregulated 64% of P1 HC genes.
source: From this analysis we determined that the iHCs had transcriptionally activated a hair cell-like signature by successfully upregulating 64% of P1 HC genes, while simultaneously becoming distinct from the starting MEF population by successfully downregulating 69% of MEF genes (Figure 2A).
evidence: RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2A

claim: iHCs successfully downregulated 69% of MEF genes.
source: From this analysis we determined that the iHCs had transcriptionally activated a hair cell-like signature by successfully upregulating 64% of P1 HC genes, while simultaneously becoming distinct from the starting MEF population by successfully downregulating 69% of MEF genes (Figure 2A).
evidence: RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2A

claim: The reprogramming efficiency of SAPG is comparable to that achieved in other direct conversion studies.
source: These percentages are comparable to those achieved in the TF-induced direct conversion of MEFs into spinal motor neurons, as well as those attained in MEF-to-cardiomyocyte and hepatocyte-to-neuron direct conversion (Ieda et al., 2010; Marro et al., 2011; Gopalakrishnan et al., 2017; Ichida et al., 2018).
evidence: Comparison to published studies via citations

claim: iHCs are more similar to primary P1 cochlear hair cells than to cerebellar granule cell precursors.
source: Principle component analysis (PCA) indicated that iHCs were more similar to primary P1 cochlear hair cells (P1 HC) than to either cerebellar granule cell precursors (CGP) (Figure 3A), secretory cells of the gut (GUT) (Figure 3B), or Merkel cells (MC) (Figure 3C), showing that they established a hair cell-specific transcriptional program and have not adopted the transcriptional profile of other Atoh1-dependent lineages.
evidence: PCA analysis shown in Figure 3A-C

claim: 73% of unique P1 HC chromatin regions are successfully opened during reprogramming.
source: Of the 13,390 peaks present uniquely in P1 HCs, 73% were successfully opened during reprogramming, while 27% were not opened during reprogramming, and an additional 18,084 peaks opened inappropriately in iHCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: ATAC-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4A

claim: 84% of MEF-specific chromatin peaks were successfully closed during reprogramming.
source: Conversely, of the 26,847 peaks unique to MEFs, 84% of peaks were successfully closed during reprogramming, 16% were not closed during reprogramming, and an additional 833 peaks were inappropriately closed during reprogramming (Figure 4A).
evidence: ATAC-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4A

claim: SAPG can convert adult tail tip fibroblasts into Atoh1-nGFP+/MyosinVIIa+/Parvalbumin+ iHCs.
source: In addition, SAPG catalyzed the expression of MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin, indicating that as in MEFs, these transcription factors can convert adult tail tip fibroblasts into Atoh1-nGFP+/MyosinVIIa+/Parvalbumin+ iHCs (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 5A and 5B

claim: SAPG converts P8 supporting cells into hair cells at a significantly greater rate than Atoh1 alone.
source: These results indicate that the combination of Six1, Atoh1, Pou4f3, and Gfi1 can convert adult tail tip fibroblasts and P8 supporting cells into induced hair cells at a significantly greater rate than Atoh1 alone.
evidence: Comparative experimental data from Figure 5

claim: iHCs exhibit highly polarized F-actin staining near the apical surface.
source: At this time, iHCs exhibited highly polarized F-actin staining as observed by well-defined labeling of Phalloidin-Rhodamine near the apical surface and a primary cilium that labels with antibody to acetylated tubulin, and is centered on the nascent cuticular plate (Figure 6A).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A

claim: iHCs possess a primary cilium centered on the nascent cuticular plate.
source: At this time, iHCs exhibited highly polarized F-actin staining as observed by well-defined labeling of Phalloidin-Rhodamine near the apical surface and a primary cilium that labels with antibody to acetylated tubulin, and is centered on the nascent cuticular plate (Figure 6A).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A

claim: Greater than 80% of iHCs that engrafted in epithelial islands exhibited highly polarized F-actin staining.
source: Greater than 80% of iHCs that engrafted in epithelial islands exhibited highly polarized F-actin staining (data not shown).
evidence: Stated as experimental observation

claim: The mean resting potential of co-cultured iHCs is −54.8 mV.
source: The mean resting potentials for primary hair cells, cocultured iHCs, and monolayer-cultured iHCs were −58.6 mV (± 6.9), –54.8 mV (± 4.1), and −50.8 mV (± 2.4), respectively (Figure 6D).
evidence: Electrophysiology data shown in Figure 6D

claim: The resting potentials of iHCs are comparable to previously reported primary hair cell resting potentials.
source: These values are comparable to previously reported primary hair cell resting potentials (Dallos, 1985; Oliver et al., 2003).
evidence: Comparison to published studies via citations

claim: Co-cultured iHCs and primary hair cells displayed overlapping magnitudes of voltage-dependent current densities.
source: Monolayer-cultured iHCs showed small current densities while the co-cultured iHCs and primary hair cells displayed overlapping magnitudes of voltage-dependent current densities (Figure 6F).
evidence: Electrophysiology data shown in Figure 6F

claim: Co-cultured iHCs and primary hair cells show similarly longer time constants for delayed onset current.
source: The delayed onset current of monolayer-cultured iHCs displayed fast time constants (Figure 6H). In contrast, the co-cultured iHCs and primary hair cells showed similarly longer time constants, indicating that their outward currents have similar activation kinetics (Figure 6H).
evidence: Electrophysiology data shown in Figure 6H

claim: iHCs rapidly incorporated FM4-64 to high levels within a 30 s time course.
source: However, iHCs rapidly incorporated FM4-64 to high levels within a 30 s time course (Figure 6I) demonstrating that iHCs possess rudimentary mechanotransduction channels with similar styryl dye uptake as in primary hair cells within the intact organ of Corti (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D) and primary hair cells from dissociated organ of Corti preparations (Figure 6J).
evidence: FM4-64 uptake assay data shown in Figure 6I

claim: Primary hair cells of the organ of Corti specifically accumulated Texas-Red conjugated gentamicin (GTTR).
source: Primary hair cells of the organ of Corti specifically accumulated Texas-Red conjugated gentamicin (GTTR), but not Texas Red (TR) alone when treated with 0.5 mM of either compound for 3 hr (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: GTTR uptake assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: MEFs transduced with a GFP-expressing control virus did not accumulate GTTR.
source: MEFs transduced with a GFP-expressing control virus did not accumulate GTTR (Figure 7A).
evidence: GTTR uptake assay data shown in Figure 7A

claim: iHCs robustly accumulated gentamicin-Texas Red (GTTR).
source: The iHCs, similarly to primary hair cells, robustly accumulated gentamicin-Texas Red (GTTR) (Figure 7B), but not Texas Red (TR) alone (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), after a 3 hr treatment at 0.5 mM.
evidence: GTTR uptake assay data shown in Figure 7B

claim: Gentamicin caused primary hair cell degeneration in a dose-dependent manner.
source: While gentamicin caused primary hair cell degeneration in a dose-dependent manner, it caused little-to-no toxicity to Hb9-RFP+ induced motor neurons generated from MEFs by transduction with Ngn2, Isl1, Lhx3, Ascl1, Brn2, and Mty1l (Son et al., 2011; Figure 7D,E).
evidence: Ototoxicity assay data shown in Figure 7D and 7E

claim: iHCs treated with gentamicin showed rapid, dose-dependent degeneration.
source: Similar to primary hair cells, iHCs treated with gentamicin showed rapid, dose-dependent degeneration (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: Ototoxicity assay data shown in Figure 7D and 7E

claim: The reprogramming efficiency using SAPG cocktail (35%) is similar to or higher than the best reprogramming strategies for other cell types.
source: The reprogramming efficiency using this SAPG cocktail (35%) is similar and in some cases higher than the best reprogramming strategies for other cell types such as cardiomyocytes with 20% efficiency (Ieda et al., 2010) and motor neurons with 10–40% efficiency (Ichida et al., 2009; Babos et al., 2019).
evidence: Comparison to published studies via citations

claim: Six1 directly targets the Atoh1 autoregulatory enhancer.
source: Six1 directly targets the Atoh1 autoregulatory enhancer, as well as other essential hair cell enhancers for Pou4f3 and Gfi1, with an increase in Six1 occupancy as hair cells differentiate with in the sensory epithelium (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2020

claim: Six1 plays a role in the maturation of hair cells by regulating key genes involved in the establishment of planar cell polarity and hair-bundle orientation.
source: Additionally, Six1 has been shown to play a role in the maturation of hair cells by regulating key genes involved in the establishment of planar cell polarity and hair-bundle orientation (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2020

claim: iHCs fail to activate important genes essential for the functional maturation of the sensory receptors in the cochlea, such as Prestin and Gata3.
source: While many of the specialized gene characteristics of the cochlear hair cells are clearly upregulated during reprogramming (Figure 2), the iHCs fail to activate other important genes essential for the functional maturation of the sensory receptors in the cochlea, such as Prestin and Gata3 (Liberman et al., 2002; Bardhan et al., 2019).
evidence: Inference from RNA-seq data and supported by citations

claim: Continuous expression of Atoh1 is known to halt hair cell maturation.
source: Second, our current strategy relies on constitutive expression of the reprogramming factors, while continuous expression of Atoh1 is known to halt hair cell maturation (Liu et al., 2012b; Liu et al., 2014a).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2012b and Liu et al., 2014a

claim: iHCs co-cultured with dissociated organ of Corti cells promoted morphological and electrophysiological maturation of iHCs.
source: In fact, we demonstrate that iHCs co-cultured with dissociated organ of Corti cells, promoted morphological and electrophysiological maturation of iHCs (Figure 6).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 6

claim: The use of Anc80-based adeno associated vectors made inner ear gene delivery feasible.
source: Recently the use of Anc80-based adeno associated vectors made inner ear gene delivery feasible (Suzuki et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2018; Tan et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Proof of concept studies have demonstrated functional recovery after administration of TMC1 gene therapy in animals carrying a mutation in the gene.
source: The proof of concept studies have demonstrated functional recovery after administration of TMC1 gene therapy in animals carrying a mutation in the gene (Yoshimura et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yoshimura et al., 2019

claim: Supporting cells have been shown to be maintained in long deafened mice.
source: Supporting cells have been shown to be maintained in long deafened mice (Oesterle and Campbell, 2009) and humans (Johnsson et al., 1981).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: Directed differentiation protocols for ESCs towards sensory hair cells are time consuming and ESC-line dependent with variable efficiency.
source: Although directed differentiation of ESCs towards the sensory hair cells have been described (Li et al., 2003; Oshima et al., 2010; Koehler et al., 2013; Ronaghi et al., 2014), these three-dimensional protocols are time consuming and the outcomes are ESC-line dependent with variable efficiency across protocols (Hiler et al., 2015; Mellough et al., 2019; Yoon et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Direct reprogramming allows for a faster and more reliable approach to produce large quantities of induced hair cell-like cells compared to directed differentiation.
source: Direct reprogramming allows for a much faster and more reliable approach to produce large quantities of induced hair cell-like cells to scale, and the monolayer culture used here overcomes several of the short-comings of directed differentiation systems presented so far, such as long culture periods (Koehler et al., 2013), and 3D cultures that are more difficult to image robotically (Breslin and O'Driscoll, 2013; van Vliet et al., 2014).
evidence: Comparison to published studies via citations and inference from experimental design

claim: iHCs are selectively vulnerable to gentamicin.
source: We demonstrated that iHCs are selectively vulnerable to gentamicin, and can be reprogrammed and cultured in microtiter plate format, providing a robotic-imaging platform for scalable monitoring of iHC survival and small-molecule screening.
evidence: Experimental data from ototoxicity assays

claim: 16 transcription factors were identified as only and/or highly expressed in the Atoh1-nGFP+ hair cell population.
source: 16 transcription factors (TFs) were identified as only and/or highly expressed in the Atoh1-nGFP+ hair cell population.
evidence: RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: Overexpression of all 16 TFs led to Atoh1-nGFP activation in 1.7% of MEFs at 14 days post infection.
source: In contrast, overexpression of all 16 TFs led to Atoh1-nGFP activation in 1.7% (± 0.3) of MEFs at 14 days post infection (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: Atoh1 alone activated the Atoh1-nGFP reporter in 5.8% of starting MEFs.
source: We observed that Atoh1 alone activated the Atoh1-nGFP reporter in 5.8% (± 1.5) of starting MEFs, while Pou4f3-alone only did so in 0.15% (± 0.03) of the starting MEFs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: The combination of Atoh1 and Pou4f3 provided 17.5% reprogramming efficiency.
source: The most significant reporter activation came from a combination of Atoh1 and Pou4f3, which provided 17.5% (± 4.4) reprogramming efficiency (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D

claim: Gfi1 combined with Atoh1 and Pou4f3 increased the reporter activation to 26.9% reprogramming efficiency.
source: Gfi1 combined with AP (APG) increased the reporter activation to 26.9% (± 5.6) reprogramming efficiency (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E

claim: The addition of Six1 to Atoh1, Pou4f3, and Gfi1 increased the reporter activation to 35.2% reprogramming efficiency.
source: A subsequent round of addition of individual TFs to this three-factor combination showed that the addition of Six1 to Atoh1, Pou4f3, and Gfi1 (SAPG) further increased the reporter activation to reach 35.2% (± 1.8) reprogramming efficiency (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F

claim: Only 50% of the Atoh1-nGFP+ cells generated by AP or APG expressed MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin.
source: In contrast, only 50% of the Atoh1-nGFP+ cells generated by AP or APG expressed MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin, indicating that most Atoh1-nGFP+ cells generated from these alternative cocktails were not hair cell-like (Figure 1D).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1D

claim: The genes successfully upregulated during reprogramming were significantly enriched for 'sensory perception of sound' and 'detection of mechanical stimulus'.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis showed that the genes successfully upregulated during reprogramming were significantly enriched for 'sensory perception of sound' and 'detection of mechanical stimulus', which revealed as three clusters of genes (Figure 2B).
evidence: GO analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2B

claim: iHCs efficiently upregulated important hair cell genes including Whirlin, Cadherin23, Espin, Bassoon, and Otoferlin.
source: However, further investigation of the Rlog count values for several key genes in each GO cluster demonstrated that the iHCs efficiently upregulated important hair cell genes including Whirlin (Whrn) involved in cell polarity, Cadherin23 (Cdh23) and Espin (Espn) important for stereocilia organization and functionality, as well as Bassoon (Bsn) and Otoferlin (Otof) required for synaptic scaffolding and synaptic vesicle signaling (Figure 2D).
evidence: RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: iHCs activated all of the initial transcription factors included in the set of 16 candidate factors, with the exception of Zfp503.
source: After looking at the expression of key hair cell genes, we determined that the iHCs had also activated all of the initial transcription factors included in the set of 16 candidate factors, with the exception of Zfp503 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D

claim: The expression profile of iHCs has drastically shifted away from the MEF signature and towards an immature hair cell-like signature.
source: Nonetheless, the expression profile of iHCs has drastically shifted away from the MEF signature and towards an immature hair cell-like signature.
evidence: Inference from PCA and RNA-seq data analysis

claim: The largest Normalized Enrichment Score was for the comparison of iHCs to P1 hair cells, indicating an enrichment for the HC gene signature.
source: The largest NES was for the comparison of iHCs to P1 hair cells (HC), indicating an enrichment for the HC gene signature, while showing lower enrichment scores, and even negative enrichment scores, for the other cell type comparisons (Figure 3D).
evidence: GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3D

claim: Most of the enhancers identified in P1 HCs are opened in iHCs.
source: These results show that most of the enhancers identified in P1 HCs are opened in iHCs.
evidence: ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4B

claim: The genes defined as putative targets of P1 HC-specific enhancers had significantly higher expression in both P1 HCs and iHCs compared to MEFs.
source: Based on our RNA-seq data, we found that the genes defined as putative targets of P1 HC-specific enhancers had significantly higher expression in both P1 HCs and iHCs compared to MEFs (Figure 4C).
evidence: Combined RNA-seq and ATAC-seq/ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4C

claim: Robust and hair cell-appropriate global changes in chromatin accessibility accompany the large shift in the transcriptional profile of iHCs.
source: These results indicate that robust and hair cell-appropriate global changes in chromatin accessibility accompany the large shift in the transcriptional profile of iHCs.
evidence: Inference from ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: With Atoh1 alone 26.8% of the total Lfng-tdTomato+ supporting cells are able to activate the primary hair cell markers MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin.
source: With Atoh1 alone 26.8% (± 7) of the total Lfng-tdTomato+ supporting cells are able to activate the primary hair cell markers MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin, while with SAPG 71.8% (± 12) of the total Lfng-tdTomato+ supporting cells are able to activate primary hair cell markers.
evidence: Experimental data from P8 supporting cell reprogramming

claim: With SAPG 71.8% of the total Lfng-tdTomato+ supporting cells are able to activate primary hair cell markers.
source: With Atoh1 alone 26.8% (± 7) of the total Lfng-tdTomato+ supporting cells are able to activate the primary hair cell markers MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin, while with SAPG 71.8% (± 12) of the total Lfng-tdTomato+ supporting cells are able to activate primary hair cell markers.
evidence: Experimental data from P8 supporting cell reprogramming

claim: Perinatal supporting cells have been shown to have a transient ability to directly transdifferentiate into hair cells in response to Atoh1.
source: Although hair cells do not regenerate in the mature mammalian cochlea, perinatal supporting cells have been shown to have a transient ability to directly transdifferentiate into hair cells in response to Atoh1 (Kelly et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012b), or loss of Notch-mediated lateral inhibition (Mizutari et al., 2013; Maass et al., 2015), however this potential is lost at very early postnatal stages (White et al., 2006; Takebayashi et al., 2007; Doetzlhofer et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2012a; Cox et al., 2014; Bramhall et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: By two weeks of age, neither Atoh1 expression, nor induction of transdifferentiation by Notch-inhibition, can induce the transdifferentiation of supporting cells to a hair cell fate.
source: Atoh1 alone can convert perinatal supporting cells into hair cells (Kelly et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012b; Yang et al., 2013), but transdifferentiation potential decreases rapidly thereafter, such that by two weeks of age, neither Atoh1 expression, nor induction of transdifferentiation by Notch-inhibition, can induce the transdifferentiation of supporting cells to a hair cell fate (Maass et al., 2015; Jiang et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: Stereocilia development involves the elaboration of a single primary, tubulin-based, cilium, known as the kinocilium.
source: Development of stereocilia involves the elaboration of a single primary, tubulin-based, cilium, known as the kinocilium, centered on a cuticular plate of F-actin filaments from which the stereocilia arise as elongated bundles of microvilli (Cotanche and Corwin, 1991; Troutt et al., 1994; Leibovici et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2005; Tarchini et al., 2016; McGrath et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: The highly polarized pattern of F-actin in iHCs is reminiscent of hair cells in both the developing cochlear and vestibular systems.
source: This highly polarized pattern is reminiscent of hair cells in both the developing cochlear and vestibular systems (Cotanche and Corwin, 1991; Troutt et al., 1994; Leibovici et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2005; Tarchini et al., 2016; McGrath et al., 2017).
evidence: Comparison to published studies via citations

claim: iHCs co-cultured with dissociated primary E13.5 organs of Corti contained polarized cuticular plates and stereocilia.
source: After two weeks of co-culture, iHCs contained polarized cuticular plates (F-actin) and stereocilia (espin-positive), and were found incorporated into the epithelial islands containing native hair cells and supporting cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 6B

claim: The input resistance of co-cultured iHCs was comparable to that of primary hair cells.
source: However, the input resistance of co-cultured iHCs (1432 ± 327 MΩ) was comparable to that of primary hair cells (1950 ± 755 MΩ) (Figure 6D).
evidence: Electrophysiology data shown in Figure 6D

claim: Primary hair cells within the intact organ of Corti rapidly and selectively accumulate the styryl dye FM4-64 within seconds.
source: Primary hair cells within the intact organ of Corti rapidly and selectively accumulate the styryl dye FM4-64 within seconds, a time frame consistent with entry of the dye through mechanotransduction channels rather than endocytosis (Lelli et al., 2009; Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and supported by citation

claim: MEFs failed to incorporate FM4-64 within the 30 s time frame.
source: In contrast, MEFs failed to incorporate FM4-64 within the 30 s time frame (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E

claim: Gentamicin is representative of a large class of highly effective aminoglycoside antibiotics that result in significant hair cell degeneration.
source: Gentamicin is representative of a large class of highly effective aminoglycoside antibiotics that result in significant hair cell degeneration (Alharazneh et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to published research

claim: iHCs did not accumulate Texas Red alone.
source: The iHCs, similarly to primary hair cells, robustly accumulated gentamicin-Texas Red (GTTR) (Figure 7B), but not Texas Red (TR) alone (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), after a 3 hr treatment at 0.5 mM.
evidence: GTTR uptake assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C

claim: Gentamicin caused little-to-no toxicity to Hb9-RFP+ induced motor neurons.
source: While gentamicin caused primary hair cell degeneration in a dose-dependent manner, it caused little-to-no toxicity to Hb9-RFP+ induced motor neurons generated from MEFs by transduction with Ngn2, Isl1, Lhx3, Ascl1, Brn2, and Mty1l (Son et al., 2011; Figure 7D,E).
evidence: Ototoxicity assay data shown in Figure 7D and 7E

claim: iHCs provide a scalable platform for detecting agents that protect against gentamicin ototoxicity.
source: Moreover, these results suggest that iHCs provide a scalable platform for detecting agents that protect against gentamicin ototoxicity.
evidence: Inference from experimental results on gentamicin toxicity

claim: Three of the four transcription factors (Atoh1, Pou4f3, and Gfi1) were previously used to induce a hair cell like-fate from mouse ES cells that had been partially differentiated into ectodermal organoids.
source: As confirmation of the importance of the four transcription factors identified in our unbiased reprogramming investigation, three of the four transcription factors, Atoh1, Pou4f3, and Gfi1, were previously used to induce a hair cell like-fate from mouse ES cells that had been partially differentiated into ectodermal organoids (Costa et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Costa et al., 2015

claim: The addition of Six1 increases reprogramming efficiency by pushing cells towards the sensory ectodermal lineage.
source: We hypothesize that the addition of Six1 increases reprogramming efficiency by pushing cells towards the sensory ectodermal lineage.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors

claim: Six1 has been reported to promote competency and progenitor-like state, as well as being an essential determinant of early sensory inner ear lineage.
source: Six1 has been reported previously to promote competency and progenitor-like state, as well as being an essential determinant of early sensory inner ear lineage (Zheng et al., 2003; Ozaki et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: The expression gradient of Six1 in the developing sensory epithelium precedes the activation of Atoh1.
source: The expression gradient of Six1 in the developing sensory epithelium precedes the activation of Atoh1 (Ahmed et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ahmed et al., 2012

claim: At perinatal times, only modest differences in gene expression are able to distinguish inner and outer hair cells of the cochlea.
source: At perinatal times, only modest differences in gene expression are able to distinguish inner and outer hair cells of the cochlea (Liu et al., 2014b), as well as vestibular vs. cochlear hair cells (Burns et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research

claim: The transcriptional profiles of postnatal day one cochlear hair cells and utricular hair cells are very similar.
source: The transcriptional profiles of postnatal day one cochlear hair cells and utricular hair cells are very similar (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: PCA analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: The transcriptional profiles of hair cells are known to change as the hair cells mature and acquire subtype specificity and functionality.
source: This time point represents an immature hair cell, and the transcriptional profiles are known to change as the hair cells mature and acquire subtype specificity and functionality (Burns et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 2019; Hoa et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Some of the distal regulatory elements that are present in P1 hair cells, but fail to open in iHCs, associate with hair cell-specific genes that also fail to be robustly expressed during reprogramming.
source: Additional bioinformatic analysis has shown that some of the relatively small group of distal regulatory elements that are present in P1 hair cells, but fail to open in iHCs, associate with hair cell-specific genes that also fail to be robustly expressed during reprogramming (data not shown).
evidence: Bioinformatic analysis mentioned but data not shown

claim: The chromatin landscape was drastically remodeled during reprogramming of MEFs to a hair cell-like state.
source: As has been documented in other reprogramming experiments (Wapinski et al., 2013; Wapinski et al., 2017; Rhee et al., 2017), the chromatin landscape was also drastically remodeled during reprogramming of MEFs to a hair cell-like state, readily opening de novo distal elements to change their chromatin to resemble P1 cochlear hair cells.
evidence: ATAC-seq data and comparison to published studies via citations

claim: There is a residual MEF signature of the chromatin landscape in iHCs.
source: Similar to the RNA sequencing results, there is a residual MEF signature of the chromatin landscape, and the failure to close down these chromatin regions may be acting as a barrier for more efficient and/or faithful reprogramming.
evidence: Inference from ATAC-seq data analysis

claim: The opening of a large number of peaks inappropriately suggests that the SAPG cocktail may lack a transcriptional repressor.
source: In addition, the opening of a large number of peaks inappropriately (peaks that occur in neither MEFs of primary P1 hair cells) suggests that our cocktail may lack a transcriptional repressor, and that these inappropriately open distal elements may provide some explanation for the low level of inappropriate gene expression (Figures 2 and 4).
evidence: Inference from ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: Induced hair cells are highly similar to their primary counterparts on transcriptional and epigenetic levels, as well as functional levels.
source: Despite these pitfalls, common to most if not all reprogramming strategies published to date (Ieda et al., 2010; Son et al., 2011; Treutlein et al., 2016; Kaminski et al., 2016; Van Pham et al., 2017), induced hair cells are highly similar to their primary counterparts on transcriptional and epigenetic levels, as well as functional levels.
evidence: Summary inference from all experimental data presented

claim: The SAPG four transcription factor combination is significantly more effective at activating the expression of hair cell genes MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin in adult tail tip fibroblasts and postnatal (P8) supporting cells when compared to Atoh1 alone.
source: We found that the SAPG four transcription factor combination is significantly more effective at activating the expression of hair cell genes MyosinVIIa and Parvalbumin in adult tail tip fibroblasts, and postnatal (P8) supporting cells, when compared to Atoh1 alone (Figure 5).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 5

claim: The demonstration that SAPG is able to convert P8 supporting cells to a hair cell-like fate highlights the potential for future gene therapy approaches for hearing loss.
source: The demonstration that SAPG is able to convert P8 supporting cells to a hair cell-like fate, highlights the potential for future gene therapy approaches for hearing loss.
evidence: Inference from experimental results on P8 supporting cell reprogramming

claim: Primary human fibroblasts taken from patients can be reprogrammed to induced pluripotent stem cells that can then be expanded and reprogrammed to a hair cell fate for patient- and disease-specific studies.
source: Primary human fibroblasts taken from patients, can be reprogrammed to induced pluripotent stem cells that can then be expanded and reprogrammed to a hair cell fate for patient- and disease-specific studies, opening the opportunity to study hearing loss mutations, ototoxicity and regenerative medicine approaches (Koch et al., 2011; Lim et al., 2016a; Lim et al., 2016b; Shi et al., 2018; Huang et al., 2019; Villanueva-Paz et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: Directed differentiation of ESCs towards sensory hair cells has been described.
source: Although directed differentiation of ESCs towards the sensory hair cells have been described (Li et al., 2003; Oshima et al., 2010; Koehler et al., 2013; Ronaghi et al., 2014), these three-dimensional protocols are time consuming and the outcomes are ESC-line dependent with variable efficiency across protocols (Hiler et al., 2015; Mellough et al., 2019; Yoon et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: The monolayer culture used for direct reprogramming overcomes several shortcomings of directed differentiation systems such as long culture periods and 3D cultures that are more difficult to image robotically.
source: Direct reprogramming allows for a much faster and more reliable approach to produce large quantities of induced hair cell-like cells to scale, and the monolayer culture used here overcomes several of the short-comings of directed differentiation systems presented so far, such as long culture periods (Koehler et al., 2013), and 3D cultures that are more difficult to image robotically (Breslin and O'Driscoll, 2013; van Vliet et al., 2014).
evidence: Comparison to published studies via citations

claim: The efficiency and reproducibility of direct reprogramming is essential for high throughput screening approaches.
source: The efficiency and reproducibility of direct reprogramming is essential for high throughput screening approaches.
evidence: General statement about the method

claim: Reprogramming does not require an iPSC intermediate.
source: Importantly, reprogramming does not require an iPSC intermediate, thus generating iHCs from human patients with known or novel genetic mutations associated with hearing loss will enable screening for new therapeutic targets and agents for the treatment of genetic causes of deafness.
evidence: Characteristic of direct reprogramming approach

claim: The direct lineage conversion of somatic cells to a hair cell-like fate provides the means to study many outstanding questions in inner ear biology.
source: The direct lineage conversion of somatic cells to a hair cell-like fate provides the means to study many outstanding questions in inner ear biology. For instance, the nature of gene regulatory logic underlying the differentiation of the variety of cochlear and vestibular hair cell types, as well as mechanisms underlying hair cell degeneration caused by ototoxins, and the numerous mutations responsible for the many types of syndromic and non-syndromic hearing loss.
evidence: Speculation about future applications
